lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The consensus Q3 revenue bar ($1.05-1.07B) is flat on Q2 ($1,065.4M) and at the bottom of what the raised FY guide implies. H1 was $1,816.4M, so $3.9-4.2B needs H2 of $2.08-2.38B, or $1.04-1.19B a quarter. Bloom beat Q2 revenue by about 30% ($1,065M vs about $823M expected) and EPS by 2x ($0.78 vs $0.39), and has beaten 7 of its last 8 quarters. Q3 EPS estimates have had 17 upward revisions and none down in three months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-28): a ~30% revenue beat and a raised FY guide went +12% after hours, then closed the window -1.85% (baseline). findings.finding: The corrected 10-Q/A (filed 2026-07-29) shows that one non-related customer was ~73% of Q2 revenue (about $780M), and that related-party revenue fell from $373M in Q1 to $2.8M in Q2. Quarterly revenue therefore rides on one or two very large deliveries; the CFO said 'one or two customers could lead our revenue in any given quarter.' If Q3 lacks a delivery of Q2's size, it can come in below a bar that was set off Q2's level.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The Q2 concentration was not disclosed until the 10-Q, and the Q2 beat was sold anyway.

findings.finding: Halliburton (released 2026-10-20) reported Q3 2026 Middle East/Asia revenue of $1.4bn, +8% sequentially, 'driven by higher activity across multiple product service lines in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait'. It guided Q4 Middle East revenue up both sequentially and year over year, and gave an early 2027 view of mid-single-digit revenue growth. SLB's Q3 base case of +3-4% sequential revenue (consensus $9.27bn, mid-guide) assumes a gradual Middle East recovery, and its Q4 view needs Middle East revenue of $2.1-2.2bn against Q2's $1.66bn. A direct peer's Saudi/Kuwait growth, landing after SLB last spoke, makes the base case more likely than the flat-Middle-East downside (-$150m revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-24): revenue beat consensus by ~3.5% with a Middle East recovery path laid out, and the stock rose +11.0% (baseline). The three prior prints moved +2.6%, -0.3% and -0.9%. Middle East-driven quarters have been the large movers.

findings.finding: Weatherford (Q3 2026, released 2026-10-20) reported MENA/Asia revenue of $447m, flat sequentially and -16% year over year. Its CEO wrote that 'recent events in the Middle East have dampened expectations of a quick recovery'. This bears on SLB's preliminary Q4 view from July (revenue above $10bn, ~24% EBITDA margin, Middle East $2.1-2.2bn = ~95% of Q4 2025, from $1.66bn in Q2), which Q4 consensus of $10.06bn / $0.80 still mirrors. The risk is that SLB trims its Q4 Middle East assumption on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q2 print SLB set the Q4 Middle East recovery path and rose +11%. That guide is what the stock has been holding on to. In the 2025 prints (former name, outside the baseline) management cut regional expectations several times, but I have no sourced reaction for them.

findings.finding: The Gulf re-escalated inside SLB's Q3. On 2026-09-01 two supertankers carrying Saudi oil were struck in the Strait of Hormuz. On ~2026-09-08 Houthi missile and drone strikes hit Saudi energy facilities and temporarily forced some operations to stop. SLB's own July downside scenario was exactly 'renewed disruption leaves Middle East revenue flat': about -$150m revenue (-1.6% vs the $9.27bn consensus) and -$75m EBITDA, roughly -$0.04 EPS against the $0.62 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Middle East revenue fell 13% sequentially, yet total revenue beat and the stock rose 11%, because the market looked through a disruption it had expected. The reported Middle East line has not been sold on its own.

findings.finding: Contract awards since the July print support the backlog and 2027 commentary on the call: four multi-year Aramco integrated well construction contracts covering 450+ wells over an initial three years (2026-09-24), a major OQEP integrated facility expansion in Oman (2026-09-22), and a 15-year TotalEnergies DrillPlan digital agreement (2026-10-08). The Aramco award points to a Saudi drilling ramp into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no cited instance of an award announcement moving the stock on a print. The +11% in July came with a forward Middle East recovery narrative of the kind these awards support.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter with Tupperware LatAm consolidated: June alone booked Ps 451m revenue and Ps 123m EBITDA (27.4% margin), and pro forma FY2025 Tupperware revenue was Ps 5.09bn. Adding organic growth of ~4% (Q2 2026 organic +4.1%) to the Q3 2025 base of Ps 3,377m gives Q3 revenue of about Ps 4.75-4.85bn, or about $268-275M at a ~17.6-17.8 Q3 average rate, against the $261.4M Benzinga consensus (+3-5%). Repeated over H2, the same arithmetic puts FY2026 at about Ps 17.7-17.9bn (+24-25%), above the top of the company's own 18-22% guide (Ps 16.81-17.38bn). That makes a beat plus a guide raise, or an explicit acknowledgement that the guide is conservative, the likely content of the release.

findings.finding: Organic margin faces three company-confirmed or proxy headwinds against a tough comp. Q3 2025 EBITDA margin was 21.4% (Jafra Mexico adj. EBITDA +31.3%). In Q2 2026 Jafra EBITDA fell 6.7%, consolidated gross margin fell 161bp to 65.5%, and management flagged higher Betterware logistics costs from Strait of Hormuz tensions. Drewry's WCI composite was $4,500/FEU on 2026-09-17 against $1,913 on 2025-09-18 (about 2.35x), with Shanghai-LA at $7,712. Betterware imports its product, so Q3/Q4 COGS carries this. Net of Tupperware's ~27% margin, consolidated margin can still clear the at-least-19% guide, so the risk is to the organic EBITDA line and to EPS, not to the full-year margin floor.
